crime_highlights: The evidence before me left me in no doubt that Ms. Cole deliberately pulled the trigger on the rifle while it was pointed at Mr. Douglas's chest, resulting in his death.
I found that Ms. Cole committed the unlawful act of shooting Mr. Douglas with a Winchester rifle
she was in a state of advanced intoxication at the time she pulled the trigger
rationale_highlights: I must take into account all of the surrounding circumstances, including the unique circumstances of Ms. Cole as an Indigenous person
the historical and systemic factors that provide context and help in the assessment of moral blameworthiness
In my view, Ms. Cole's moral blameworthiness is high, but it is attenuated by her degree of intoxication at the time of the offence and her background and circumstances.
note: Effect also stated at para 49; victim death only in para 1 and 4.

rationale_highlights: to what extent systemic or background factors, as described in Gladue and Ipeelee, operated in any way in the offender's life or affected his moral culpability for this crime
Mr. Henry has experienced many of the intergenerational effects of the Residential School System
I am satisfied there are strong Gladue factors present here which should bear on the determination of what is a fit and appropriate sentence for Mr. Henry in this case.
considering the strong Gladue factors present here and the mitigating factor that Mr. Henry pleaded guilty, albeit on the first day of trial

rationale_highlights: systemic and background factors may bear on an offender's culpability to the extent they shed light on the level of moral blameworthiness
they may diminish moral culpability and must be considered to ensure proportionality
Both of Mr. Dennis's parents were residential school survivors.
I also accept that further support comes from the connection between Mr. Dennis's crimes and the Indigenous sentencing factors present in his upbringing.
note: Court's conclusion is brief: factors support the joint submission of 10 years parole ineligibility.
